name: an absent field fails every ordering comparison, rather than reading as zero
why: The two implementations disagreed here and nothing caught it. `Number(null)` is 0 in JavaScript — not NaN — so a missing field slipped past the finite check and was ordered as if it had been measured at zero, passing `lt` and `lte` on nothing at all. Rust already returned false, because its coercion drops nulls. The case matters because absent is now ordinary: `file` reports `sizeBytes: null` and `modifiedSecondsAgo: null` for a path that is not there, so a freshness threshold would have called a missing file freshly written. It was never specific to those targets — `$.queue.depth lt 100` over a response that omitted the field has always read as an empty queue.
